scope: Introductory summaries of existing verified results, not new theorem statements or new proof obligations.

geometry.latex:
% BEGIN VERIFIED OVERVIEW geometry
For the following equality and stability statements, take John coordinates
$J(K)=B_2^n$, assume $n\ge2$, and write
$H_v=\{x:v^Tx\le0\}$ with $\|v\|=1$. Here $B_2^n$ is the Euclidean unit ball.
Put $b=1/n$ and $P=I-vv^T$. The extremal ellipsoid and contact set are
\[
\begin{gathered}
c_*=-\frac12v,\qquad
A_*=\frac12vv^T+\frac1{\sqrt{1-b}}P,\qquad
\mathcal E_*=c_*+A_*B_2^n,\\
\mathcal Z_b=\{-v\}\cup\{u:\|u\|=1,\ u^Tv=b\}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm-equality} states that equality holds if and only if
$\mathcal E_*\subseteq K$ and $K$ admits a supporting John frame whose
contacts lie in $\mathcal Z_b$. John frames are
the positive-weight contact decompositions defined in Section~\ref{sec:john-frames}.
At equality, $J(K\cap H_v)=\mathcal E_*$, and every positive-weight John frame
supporting $K$ has this pole-and-latitude geometry. The containment condition
leaves freedom in the rest of the body, giving extremizers beyond regular simplices.

For any feasible cut ellipsoid
$\mathcal E(c,A)=c+AB_2^n\subseteq K\cap H_v$, with $A$ symmetric positive
definite, suppose that its deficit satisfies
\[
0\le\epsilon:=\log\frac{R_n}{\det A}\le10^{-6}.
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm-stability} gives the explicit, dimension-independent estimates
\[
\|A-A_*\|_F\le30\sqrt\epsilon,\qquad
\|c-c_*\|\le50\sqrt\epsilon,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i\operatorname{dist}(u_i,\mathcal Z_b)^2
\le\frac{1024}{3}\epsilon,
\]
where the matrix norm is Frobenius and $(u_i,\lambda_i)$ is any supporting
John frame of $K$. Thus near equality controls the ellipsoid and the original
weighted contacts without selecting a unique extremal body. Section~\ref{sec:eq-stability}
proves the full classification and all stability estimates.
% END VERIFIED OVERVIEW geometry
geometry.domain: Normalized convex body, n >= 2, unit v; any positive-definite feasible cut ellipsoid with 0 <= epsilon <= 10^-6; every positive-weight supporting John frame.
geometry.correspondence: The model and contact set are the original definitions. For normalized convex K, E_star subset K implies conv(B union E_star) subset K, while a supporting frame implies K subset P_U; hence the equality summary is the original sandwich iff. The three displayed stability estimates are exactly the geometric components of Theorem 6.2, with unchanged threshold and constants.

optimization.latex:
% BEGIN VERIFIED OVERVIEW optimization
\paragraph{Certificates and optimization.}
On a bounded full-dimensional polytope $\mathcal P$ in any positive dimension,
the ellipsoid problem maximizes $\log\det A$ under second-order-cone support constraints.
For a normalized primal--dual feasible pair, with ellipsoid $\mathcal E(c,A)$
and positive-definite dual aggregate $M$, the computable gap satisfies
\[
G=-\log\det M-\log\det A\ge0,\qquad
\operatorname{vol}\mathcal E(c,A)\ge e^{-G}w(\mathcal P).
\]
The normalization and feasibility conditions are given in
Section~\ref{sec:2.2}; the relative-volume guarantee is established in
Section~\ref{sec:7.3}. It supplies a stopping criterion for an ellipsoid
subproblem. For central cuts in dimensions at least two, our explicit certificate bounds the new optimum
from the original John contacts, without requiring the unknown recomputed
ellipsoid. The exact deficit identity in Proposition~\ref{prop-gap} then
separates the geometric determinant loss from the optimization gap.
This connects the sharp contraction analysis with certifiable ellipsoid
computation. Exact duality and contact recovery are proved in
Section~\ref{sec:2.3}.
% END VERIFIED OVERVIEW optimization
optimization.domain: Bounded full-dimensional polytope in a positive dimension, normalized primal-dual feasible pair. The explicit central-cut construction is stated for dimensions at least two.
optimization.correspondence: The gap is the original normalized primal-dual gap and the volume guarantee is the existing relative-volume stopping criterion. The prose distinguishes optimization accuracy from geometric determinant loss; no faster centering or total arithmetic bound is claimed.
